record.context_brief: Perfect GO-spaces and sigma-closed-discrete dense sets
record.original_question: Let kappa be a cardinal greater than omega_1. A generalized ordered space, or GO-space, is a linearly ordered set equipped with a Hausdorff topology having a base of order-convex sets; a linearly ordered topological space, or LOTS, is the special case where the topology is the open-interval topology of the order. Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space with local density at most kappa has a sigma-closed-discrete dense set? Equivalently, is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect non-Archimedean space with local density at most kappa is metrizable, or that every perfect GO-space with local density at most kappa and a point-countable base is metrizable?

evidence.quote: A generalized ordered space (a GO-space) is a triple (X, τ, <) where (X, <) is a linearly ordered set and τ is a Hausdorff topology on X that has a base of order-convex sets.

Question 1. Let κ > ω1 be a cardinal number. Is it consistent with ZFC that any perfect GO-space with local density ≤ κ must have a σ-closed-discrete dense set? Equivalently, is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect non-Archimedean space with local density ≤ κ is metrizable? Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space with local density ≤ κ and with a point-countable base is metrizable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $(X,<)$ is a linearly ordered set and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ that has a base consisting of order-convex sets (a set $C\subseteq X$ is order-convex if $a,b\in C$ and $a<x<b$ imply $x\in C$). A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a GO-space whose topology coincides with the open-interval topology induced by $<$. A topological space is perfect if every closed subset is a $G_\delta$. A space has local density at most $\kappa$ if every point has a neighborhood of density at most $\kappa$. A subset $D\subseteq X$ is $\sigma$-closed-discrete if it is a countable union of subsets each of which is closed and discrete in $X$. A topological space is non-Archimedean if it has a base $\mathcal B$ such that any two members of $\mathcal B$ are either disjoint or one contains the other. A space has a point-countable base if it admits a base $\mathcal B$ such that every point belongs to at most countably many members of $\mathcal B$.

Question. Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal with $\kappa>\omega_1$. Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space of local density at most $\kappa$ has a $\sigma$-closed-discrete dense subset? Equivalently, is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect non-Archimedean space of local density at most $\kappa$ is metrizable, and is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space of local density at most $\kappa$ admitting a point-countable base is metrizable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a known program of Bennett and Lutzer on perfect GO-spaces with $\sigma$-closed-discrete dense subsets. It is known that the property is axiom-sensitive (independent of ZFC for small cardinalities), and there is no published evidence that the consistency question for $\kappa>\omega_1$ has been resolved. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: GO-spaces with σ-closed discrete dense subsets
status_evidence.snippet: Whether every perfect GO-space has a σ-closed-discrete dense set is axiom-sensitive and undecidable for spaces of small cardinality.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of σ-closed-discrete dense subsets in perfect GO-spaces is independent of ZFC for small cardinalities, indicating the consistency question at higher cardinals remains studied and unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress in the Topology of Generalized Ordered Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Survey by Bennett and Lutzer of progress on GO-spaces and related open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys discuss the open status of structural questions about perfect GO-spaces and σ-closed-discrete dense sets.
